text:
Jake Sanderson's season really started on Oct. 21. He played 4.5 minutes of the opener in Toronto and didn't dress again until then, and since returning he has nine assists and a goal in nine games while logging 22.7 minutes a night. A Senators video this month was titled "Top D Pair Looks to 'Keep Building' on Strong Play."

The points are a little ahead of the underlying numbers. His 5v5 expected-goal share is a flat 50%, 3.4 points worse than Ottawa without him, and our wins-added measure ranks him low because so little of his production is goals. His talent range puts him near 1.9 points per 60; he's at 2.65, and he has gone three games without a point.

But this is a 24-year-old Evolving-Hockey ranked fifth among 215 defensemen last season at 3.3 wins, with 3.2 goals of value from drawing more penalties than he takes. He also reaches dangerous ice more than almost any defenseman (96th percentile in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking). Our projection: 57 points.
headline: Sanderson's assists arrived once he did
